Map of Housing Lotteries / Where to Apply for Affordable Housing in NYC

Back before everything was on the internet, they used to list these housing opportunities in the classified section of the Times, Post and Daily News.

My mom was eager to get me out of the house, so she faithfully clipped each listing and sat at the kitchen table making sure I applied to each.

I sent out dozens.

Then I waited. It took a very long time.

As a result, I scored a $600 apartment in a Times Square luxury building, got offers to live in Chelsea for $580, got offers to live in the same building as Preppy Killer Robert Chambers for $688, and several more.

A few years after I was in Times Square, I got my decade-old application approved for an affordable East Village co-op.

My advice to anyone is to apply to each one you qualify for, then forget about it. Years later, you'll get an approval notice for something you barely remember applying for.
